title: Values at k distinct inputs determine a polynomial of degree less than k
summary: Over the same field, each Lagrange denominator is a difference of input coordinates. It is invertible when the coordinates are distinct.
applies: Finite field polynomials and sampling with errors
detail: Restoring f(0) in the prime domain allows the interpolation basis function to be evaluated directly at 0 without first converting to real numbers.
boundary: Repeating the abscissa does not add an independent constraint; if the points may be damaged, randomly selecting k points cannot guarantee that the original polynomial can be obtained.
relevance: Polynomial slicing explains which value of the secret is to be recovered.
